first_frame: Cinematic 16:9 natural-history film still, the opening frame of a documentary. A single tiny primitive four-toed horse (Sifrhippus) stands alone on a humid Eocene forest floor carpeted with enormous fallen leaves, seen from the side at ground level from 3 metres away: a fox-sized horse with a reddish-brown coat and faint pale dapples, a short neck, a small head with small upright ears, slender legs, a short tufted tail. It is dwarfed by its surroundings: giant fern fronds, a mossy fallen log, fallen leaves longer than its body. Hazy golden light falls through a dense subtropical canopy in soft volumetric shafts; warm humid haze hangs in the air. The horse stands in the left third of the frame facing right, fully visible from ears to hooves, with open leaf-covered ground ahead of it to walk into. Photorealistic natural-history documentary recreation, BBC/NatGeo grade, long lens, shallow depth of field, subtle film grain, restrained cinematic grade. ONE SINGLE FULL-FRAME 16:9 PHOTOGRAPH - not a grid, collage, contact sheet or split-screen. The photograph fills the entire 16:9 frame edge to edge with NO black bars, NO letterboxing, NO pillarboxing, no border and no matte of any kind. No inset picture, no picture-in-picture panel, no camera HUD, no timestamp. No text, letters, words, subtitles or captions anywhere in frame. No people.
